title: Shortcut review
summary: Practise the key navigation, selection, fill and formatting shortcuts without being told the keys.
intro:
In this review we only describe the task, and you have to remember the shortcut. If you forget one, ask for a hint or go back to the shortcuts page.

Repetition turns a shortcut into a habit: after a few days of use you will press it without thinking.

faq.q: What is the best way to learn shortcuts?
faq.a: Use two or three in your real work every day, rather than memorising a long list at once. Add more once the first ones have become habits.

faq.q: Do these shortcuts work in Excel in other languages?
faq.a: Yes. Shortcuts follow the position of the keys, so they work whatever language your keyboard is set to. On a right-to-left sheet, only the arrows are mirrored.

review-back-to-top.prompt: You are on row 800 of the table. Go back to cell `A1` with a single shortcut.
review-back-to-top.hint: Ctrl with the key that means the start.

review-select-row-to-end.prompt: Select from the current cell to the last filled cell in the row, towards column Z.
review-select-row-to-end.hint: The selection key, the jump key and the arrow.

review-fill-down.prompt: Copy the formula from the first cell of the selection into the cells below it.

review-autosum.prompt: Insert AutoSum in the cell below the column of numbers.
review-autosum.hint: On Windows: Alt with the equals sign.

review-bold.prompt: Make the selected column headings bold.

review-undo.prompt: You pasted in the wrong place. Undo your last action.

review-select-row.prompt: Select the whole row of the current cell so you can format it.

review-lock-reference.prompt: The cursor is on the reference `E1` inside a formula. Lock it so it becomes `$E$1`.
